key_insight: Decoder-only LLMs exhibit systematic and distinct failure modes when translating gender-ambiguous source text into gender-marked target languages; a focused diagnostic evaluation reveals sensitivity to prompt context, model size, and formulation that standard benchmarks miss.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of fine-grained evaluation for gender disambiguation in machine translation, specifically diagnosing how decoder-only architectures convert implicit gender cues into explicit, gender-marked target forms and where they systematically fail or amplify bias.
method: Construct a controlled diagnostic benchmark of gender-ambiguous source sentences and target languages that require explicit gender marking (varying occupations, pronouns, and contextual cues).

Evaluate decoder-only models using targeted protocols: prompt variations, explicit context injection, and model-size comparisons; measure accuracy, bias amplification, and calibration for gender choices.
Analyze failure modes and sensitivities (e.g., context length, prompt phrasing, language pairs) to produce reproducible diagnostics and recommendations for evaluation practice.
impact: Provides practitioners with a focused evaluation toolkit to detect and quantify gender-disambiguation failures in decoder-only MT systems, informing safer deployment, prompt design, and targeted mitigation strategies.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset → prompt/context variations → decoder-only model → gender-marked translations (high-level flow).
Bar chart comparing translation accuracy by gender category and prompt condition across model sizes.
Side-by-side examples: original ambiguous source, model outputs under different prompts/contexts, annotated error types.
Heatmap matrix: error rates by source language constructions vs. target-language gender marking requirements.
paper_title: Gender Disambiguation in Machine Translation: Diagnostic Evaluation in Decoder-Only Architectures
paper_authors: Chiara Manna, Hosein Mohebbi, Afra Alishahi, Frédéric Blain, Eva Vanmassenhove
